## Afternoon — Quantum Computing: Technology, Resources and Policy

### Doru Tanasa

**Title:** From scientific excellence to industrial leadership: Europe's path towards the Quantum Act

**Institution:** DG CNECT, European Commission

Doru Tanasa holds a PhD in Computer Science. He works at the European Commission since 2015, now as a Team Leader in the unit C2, DG CNECT. The unit C2 deals with Quantum Technologies.

### Rene Chatwell

**Title:** Deploying a world-class European quantum computing infrastructure

**Institution:** EuroHPC Joint Undertaking

Rene holds a PhD in Physics from the Technical University of Berlin (2021). They gained experience implementing national HPC, AI, and QC strategy as a Research Officer at the German Aerospace
Centre's (DLR) project management branch (2020–2022). Since 2023, they have been serving as the Programme Manager for Quantum Computing at the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking, overseeing quantum system
procurement and managing quantum-specific R&I grants.

### Kyriacos Hatzaras

**Title:** Quantum Computing for Health in Europe: An Overview

**Institution:** DG CNECT, European Commission

He works at the European Commission, Directorate-General CNECT (Communication Networks, Content and Technology), in the digital health / AI-in-health space.
He is a senior member of Unit A6, AI in Health & Life Sciences, at the European AI Office within DG CNECT, focused on digital health and advanced technology policy.

### Vito Palmisano

**Title:** The Quantum Landscape - State of the Art, Architectures and Installations

**Institution:** Quantum & HPC Engineer, CINECA, Italy

Vito Palmisano is an engineer specializing in Data Science and Quantum Computing
within CINECA's Quantum Computing Lab. He focuses on the integration of quantum
systems with HPC infrastructures, participating in national and European projects
related to benchmarking, software development, and Quantum Machine Learning
applications.
